entry.title: Building Smarter Virtual Wallets: The Next Frontier for Fintech Developers
entry.summary: Virtual wallets are quickly becoming one of the most exciting spaces in fintech — and for developers, they open up endless possibilities. Beyond just holding money, virtual wallets are evolving into full financial ecosystems that can handle payments, savings, identity, and even cross-border transactions in real time. Why Virtual Wallets Matter for Developers Developers are the ones turning digital finance from an idea into reality. With the right APIs, it’s now possible to: Build wallet features directly into apps or platforms Enable peer-to-peer transfers and merchant payments Manage multi-currency balances and instant conversions Integrate with global payment networks for reach and compliance The real magic lies in interoperability — connecting wallets across borders and ecosystems. That’s where companies like Thunes come in, offering APIs that let developers link with over 120 wallet brands and reach billions of users worldwide. Key Tech Drivers API-first infrastructure: Makes wallet integration faster and more modular. Tokenization & encryption: Keep transactions secure without slowing them down. Scalable cloud systems: Support high-volume, low-latency financial operations. Regulatory automation: Built-in KYC and AML compliance layers streamline onboarding. The Opportunity As users demand more seamless digital payment experiences, developers are shaping what “money” feels like in the digital age. Virtual wallets are no longer just fintech tools — they’re becoming the operating systems for financial interaction. If you’re building for fintech, commerce, or digital identity, now’s the time to start experimenting with wallet APIs. The next big leap in global finance will be written in code.

entry.title: Linux Commands — nohup, Zip & Disk Management
entry.summary:
nohup and Background Process
nohup (short for no hang up) is used to run a command or program in the background. The process continues even if you close the terminal tab.
It stops when you shut down the system.
Without nohup, closing the terminal will terminate the process.
Command Description
nohup program_file Runs the given program in the background.
nohup program_file >> storing_file Runs the program in the *background and stores the output in another file (storing_file). *(Press Enter twice to continue)
top Displays all currently running processes.
ps Shows the status of active processes (Process Status).
ps -aux Lists detailed information about all running processes.
cat storing_file Displays the entire log content of a stored background process.
tail -f storing_file Shows the last 10 lines and updates live as new logs appear.
tail -10 storing_file Displays only the last 10 lines of the file.
kill -9 process_id Forcefully stops a process using its process ID (find it using ps -aux).
grep file_name Searches for a matching pattern inside a specific file.
Command Description
sudo apt install zip Installs the zip package.
zip zip_name.zip file_name Compresses a single file.
zip -r zip_name.zip folder_name Compresses a folder recursively (includes all sub-files and directories).
unzip zip_name.zip Extracts the contents of a zip file.
Command Description
df -h Displays the disk space usage of all drives (in human-readable format).
du -sh Shows how much disk space a particular file or directory uses.
Quick Summary Use nohup to run programs in the background safely.
Use ps, top, and kill to manage processes.
Use zip and unzip for file compression.
Use df and du to monitor disk usage.
